newsitem.title: USA: U.S. State Department said faltering on science.
newsitem.headline: U.S. State Department said faltering on science.

text.p: The U.S. State Department is ill-equipped to foster necessary international cooperation on key science and technology ventures, a former cabinet member wrote on Thursday.

"Unfortunately, the State Department today has neither the human resources, organisational structure, culture, nor funds to facilitate (science and technology) bilateral or multilateral efforts," former Energy Secretary James Watkins wrote in the current edition of the journal Science.

Watkins, who served in the cabinet from 1989 through 1993, said the situation has deteriorated since 1992, when an independent report by the Carnegie Commission criticised Washington's lack of a "balanced strategy for issues at the intersection of science and technology with foreign affairs."

Without State Department support for such large-scale projects as the superconducting super collider, the thermonuclear experimental reactor and conventions on climate change and biodiversity, international participation withers, Watkins wrote.

"State Department involvement, understanding and support today can offer the best hope of funding success tomorrow, but leadership there always seems to be lacking in both timely enthusiasm and technical qualifications," Watkins wrote.
